title: ICE Busts Massive OPT Fraud Ring, 10,000 Foreign Students Under Scrutiny
excerpt: Homeland Security uncovers nationwide network of phantom employers and shell companies, many operated from India, exploiting student visa program
body:
**Phantom Jobs, Real Consequences**

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement has uncovered what officials call one of the largest student visa fraud operations in American history — a sprawling network of over 10,000 foreign students employed by phantom companies under the Optional Practical Training program. ICE Director Todd M. Lyons announced the findings at a press conference on Monday.

Investigators found shell companies operating from empty buildings with locked doors, offshore payroll systems, and coordinated employer clusters designed to give the appearance of legitimate STEM employment. Many of the fraudulent companies were traced to operations run from India, according to federal officials.

**A Program Under Siege**

The OPT program allows F-1 visa holders to work in the U.S. for up to 12 months after graduation, with STEM graduates eligible for a 36-month extension. The program has grown dramatically in recent years and become a critical pathway for Indian students seeking H-1B sponsorship. But investigators say it has also become a magnet for fraud, with employers filing false training plans and students paying for fictitious work experience.

The crackdown comes as international student enrollment in the U.S. has already dropped 20% in 2026 amid broader visa restrictions and policy uncertainty under the Trump administration.

nri_angle: Indian students are the largest group of OPT participants in America — this crackdown directly threatens the F-1 to H-1B pipeline that tens of thousands of Indian graduates depend on each year.
author: Diaspora Desk
